groups.defect: The fire-and-forget legacy-write goroutines in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection build their timeout context from the request context. That context is canceled when the handler returns, so legacy writes silently abort with context.Canceled. The fix is to detach with context.WithoutCancel.

answer.reasoning: All four suggestions anchor at dualwriter_mode3.go lines 50-57. Each one names the same defect: the goroutines derive their context from the request context through context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). Each one lists all four goroutine sites (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection) and gives the same fix, context.WithoutCancel. s_85cdb7f9 also mentions the playlist integration tests and the unit tests that use context.Background(). It does this to explain why the bug isn't caught, not to report a separate defect, so its membership is unaffected. Whether these four belong together is clear. The kind is not. The defect repeats at four places, which looks like systemic_pattern, but every member already covers all four sites and anchors at the same lines. Any single member's comment therefore covers everything, which points to same_location with no unified comment needed. Because the kind is a judgment call, decisive is false.
